doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Joining and playing with Miles Davis
title: Sorting out the 1968 discography: Evans, Lloyd, and Miles's Directions
summary: Brown and DeJohnette reconcile 1968 sessions and a Teo Macero percussion credit.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Now that I got the discography back up I’m seeing a few dates with Bill Evans; Live at The Village Vanguard and also what you said earlier, the Live at Montreux.
The Live at The Village Vanguard?
This one was a later one; let me see when it was released. It was recorded August of…

Well it may have been a bootleg but then it was released on Milestone Records. This is New York in August of 68’ and for the record let me go ahead and… …and it’s reflecting also that you did a town hall concert with Charles Lloyd in November of 68.’

And then the next recording in the discography is the Miles Davis session. The “Directions” session and that was actually November not September as I said earlier. And you’re correct: Joe Zawinul, Herbie and Chick are all on that so it looks like the precursor to “Bitches Brew.” It’s also crediting Teo Macero with playing percussion. Do you recall that?
I don’t know, I don’t remember that. Maybe, I don’t know maybe he was. I thought he was in the control room.
Maybe he was tapping on something, who knows?
Maybe he overdubbed. I don’t know.
